title: KLiNQ: Knowledge Distillation-Assisted Lightweight Neural Network for Qubit Readout on FPGA
problem: Qubit readout in superconducting quantum processors is slow and error-prone; current neural-network approaches require large, resource-intensive models and lack support for mid-circuit measurements critical for quantum error correction.
motivation: High-fidelity qubit readout enabling mid-circuit measurements is essential for practical quantum error correction, but current methods consume excessive hardware resources and cannot support the rapid independent readouts needed.
method: KLiNQ uses knowledge distillation to compress neural networks to 99% smaller size while maintaining 91% qubit-state discrimination accuracy. Each qubit gets a dedicated compact neural network on Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGA, enabling independent 32-ns readouts.
key_novelty: Knowledge distillation-compressed neural networks achieving 99% model size reduction while maintaining accuracy and enabling rapid independent qubit readouts for mid-circuit measurements.
contributions: Knowledge distillation approach reducing neural network size by 99% for qubit readout
99% model size reduction maintaining 91% qubit-state discrimination accuracy
32-ns independent qubit readout enabling mid-circuit measurements on UltraScale+ FPGA implementation

metrics.other: 99% model size reduction; 32 ns readout latency

limitations: Scalability to larger qubit arrays and robustness across qubit parameter variations not discussed.
primary_theme: Compressed neural networks for efficient qubit readout
